note_en: The English edition of the errata register. It is the same register: one summary per entry id, in the order the entries are published. The Chinese what/why/fix fields and every entry's commit join live in errata.json beside this file, which points here by path.

summaries.E01: Two machine-readable references pointed at feature ids that do not exist — `BUILDING-001` and `LANDUSE-001` against the real `BLDG-001` and `LU-001`.
summaries.E02: ”less than half the second-thinnest track” did not hold arithmetically: 14 against 28 is exactly half.
summaries.E03: Six of twelve scenario cards wrote the benchmark as `BM-2x` or `BM-3xx` — placeholders, not ids, joining to no point in the shipped geometry.
summaries.E04: The English card table silently dropped the spatial-anchor column while its own opening sentence declared that column mandatory.
summaries.E05: Three structural conclusions at the end of `verify.js` were `console.log` only and never reached the exit code — flip `official_boundary` to true and it printed the problem and passed.
summaries.E06: Two of three named constraints were referenced nowhere in the package, and the third was cited four times against the wrong feature.
summaries.E07: A class-1 metrics table still carried 82,413 m² while the same document, two hundred lines away, called that value superseded.
summaries.E08: 369.3 ha was attributed to a single feature that is 192.9 ha on its own; 369.3 is the total of three.
summaries.E09: The third phase layer contained 96.44% of the second, double-counting 40% of the area — the phasing expressed no sequence at all.
summaries.E10: A closing route self-intersected: the straight return to the origin crossed two of its own earlier legs, one of them within 6 m of a benchmark.
summaries.E11: Three benchmarks had no walkable connection to the spine — 501 m, 323 m and 59.8 m away — joined only by survey chords, in a proposal whose argument is that anyone can walk up to one.
summaries.E12: Three buildings stood on land uses that contradict their own type, the worst a 7,820 m² mobility hub sitting entirely inside park green space.
summaries.E13: `non_ai_path_available` was not required by the schema and the checker rejected only an explicit false — omitting the field passed, so the AI-off guarantee could be satisfied by silence.
summaries.E14: The census front-matter parser read inline arrays only and could not see YAML block lists, so four proposals' declared tracks were never counted by any run.
summaries.E15: ”Origin datum” was attached to the wrong benchmark: in surveying it is the point heights are transferred *from*, which here is BM-0, as the package's own closure checker already enforced.
summaries.E16: A closing route is checkable because it ends on a second independently known point, and the checker verified the start and never the end.
summaries.E17: The 412.5 m reading, cited eight times, could not be recomputed by a reviewer: the package shipped the derived scalar and not the coordinates, and the measuring script lived outside it.
summaries.E18: `sources.json` said the package no longer redistributes the source database. Shipping OSM coordinates made that false the moment it was done — an extracted subset is an ODbL derivative.
summaries.E19: The A3 cover overprinted its own contents, the disclaimer sat on another line, the frame rule ran between two rows and the last line fell outside the frame — while `overflow_qa` reported zero, because it compared text against the frame and this was text against text.
summaries.E20: Every A0 board was 38% blank: three sheets to a board are height-constrained, so each used 62% of the width available to it.
summaries.E21: The HTML report never parsed block quotes or bold, so the opening epigraph rendered as a run-on sentence with a literal `>` and 1,168 literal asterisks printed across the document.
summaries.E22: The offline page kept a third hand-copied set of scenario cards, still carrying placeholder benchmark ids the rest of the package had already fixed, and a drawing list frozen at nine sheets while twelve shipped.
summaries.E23: The manifest declared `data_confidence: medium` at the top level and `high` inside `validation_claim` — one file, two confidences.
summaries.E24: A metrics table headed “all class-1 values” listed seven of nine; two metrics were added to `metrics.json` and never to the hand-built table.
summaries.E25: A route legend still showed the closing tail that had been removed from the geometry two days earlier.
summaries.E26: A hierarchy table listed the origin among the first-order points while the legend four lines below, on the same sheet, distinguished them correctly.
summaries.E27: A land-use legend listed six classes against a seven-class partition, and the map silently drew the seventh through its unknown-code fallback as grey “other”.
summaries.E28: A sheet footer disclaimed a reading of 0.86 as illustrative while the plate drawn above it showed 0.26 — a caveat protecting a number that was not on the sheet.
summaries.E29: A sheet said PR numbers had passed 900 when they had passed 1,000, on a branch whose own PR was #1065.
summaries.E30: The manifest and the rights ledger both counted 80 files while the copyright statement said 77, and its own category table also totalled 77.
summaries.E31: The census-claims gate asked only whether the current value appeared somewhere, so it could not see the same quantity written as an older value elsewhere in the document.
summaries.E32: ”The matcher in #957 is an empty set on the historical corpus — 1,203 actions, 0 matches, so it will never fire”. All 1,203 came from an older prompt that never asked for the prefix being counted; measuring a token's rate in a corpus that never required it can only return zero.
summaries.E33: `overflow_qa` measured every run against the frame rule while its own error text said “footer rule” — the check and its message named different lines.
summaries.E34: A figure called land-use-structure contained no land-use structure: it drew the three scope levels and the benchmark orders instead.
summaries.E35: The list of files the reviewing model receives was read wrong in three ways, in the measurement built to establish what the reviewer actually sees.
summaries.E36: Four compliance-matrix references all resolved and all pointed at the wrong section — each to the chapter answering the *next* requirement. Resolution is not aim.
summaries.E37: The narrative opened with 228 proposals, 69 undisclosed, 84 strings, 9 model families, and the assumption register agreed — while the corpus had long since become 354 / 106 / 113 / 8.
summaries.E38: The sheet titled “three key areas and benchmark layout” drew the three key areas as three empty dashed boxes — one of the five figures the reviewer always receives, and the deliverable for the taskbook's detailed-design requirement.
summaries.E39: A new build step read the shipped *copy* of the field map while the step that refreshes that copy ran after it, so a census that had moved was reported from the stale one.
summaries.E40: Repeated reviews of one head SHA were treated as a repeatability measurement of the review instrument, when the queue's cache did not check model, endpoint or reasoning effort — so the repeat may have been the same answer served twice.
summaries.E41: A comment claimed seven font copies would collapse into one. Measured: fourteen embedded font programs and 10.54 MB of uncompressed glyph data, six distinct Regulars and six distinct Bolds.
summaries.E42: The land-use table listed six classes against a seven-class partition in the shipped geometry; the missing one was the station-concourse connection, in both languages at once.
summaries.E43: An eleven-column table's separator was written as eleven `|---|` cells run together, parsing to 21 fields against an 11-column header, so no renderer draws it as a table.
summaries.E44: A reference audit found anchors that resolve and point the wrong way — the referent exists and the direction is wrong, which no existence check can see.
summaries.E45: ”Across 351 proposals there is not one erratum” was measured once and then quoted from memory; re-measured it was false.
summaries.E46: ”The placeholder count held at 107 across the last four readings” — recovered from this branch's own history, one of those readings was 105, the run was three not four, and the numerator had fallen while the sentence claimed stability.
summaries.E47: Twenty-two of forty-four evidence summaries appended “independently recomputed by verify.js” to every metric they named, while that script recomputes only the seventeen marked class 1 — a file credited with work it declines to do.
summaries.E48: The front matter said twelve repeatable censuses had been run while the reading log held fourteen, and the body said fourteen twice.
summaries.E49: Two sources were graded `official_context` while both carried `source_type: agent_inferred_from_public_data` — the evidence class outranked the provenance it rested on.
summaries.E50: The wall built to display this network's own failures stood where the institution stands, about 3 km from the community point where inconsistent readings actually land. **Bad news belongs where it happened.**
summaries.E51: An eleven-column table declared a 21-field separator and stopped rendering as a table, directly beneath the sentence asserting every column was mandatory — in the English edition only.
summaries.E52: The sheet frame prints the other language's title opposite the figure number, and every string passes through the translator — so each English sheet printed its own English title twice and never the Chinese one.
summaries.E53: The type-width table used to lay out every drawing carried estimates of 0.52 em lowercase; measured against the actual font with fontTools it is 0.572, so every line had been laid out against a width the font does not have.
summaries.E54: `overflow_qa` kept its own copy of that width table. The previous erratum corrected the one in `figures.py` and not the one in the gate, so the gate judged overruns by the numbers the fix had just replaced.
summaries.E55: The cover truncated over-long titles to the column width — truncating the *Chinese* title, while English is substituted afterwards and runs about 80% longer, so “truncated” titles ran into the next column.
summaries.E56: The kit of parts had a column headed “the hard constraint a fabricator could fail” and not one entry carried a number: flush with no tolerance, seating with no height, guidance with no width. **The package contained no millimetre at all.**
summaries.E57: A hard constraint was written in a form nothing could be judged against: it could not be failed, so it measured nothing.
summaries.E58: Work that was finished and shipped was left unreachable from the argument it exists to support.
summaries.E59: Asking E58's question of every shipped file: of 106 files, 21 were never named in either edition, and seven of those are products a reviewer could open — both PDFs, both rendered reports, the offline page and two datasets.
summaries.E60: This proposal argues repeatedly that review you must walk fifteen minutes to reach has not been given, and had never measured its own walk: 1,111 m at the worst point, 30.9 minutes for a wheelchair user — twice the limit it holds others to.
summaries.E61: The reading plate printed a tolerance in millimetres while the contract defines the quantity as a dimensionless rate.
summaries.E62: Asking E61's question of every drawing script found the same shape again: a number in a drawing and the same number in shipped data, drifting because only one was checked.
summaries.E63: KIT-01 requires the stone flush with no trip hazard, and a mark set flush into level paving sits in whatever the paving collects. Frozen, the thing specified so nobody would trip becomes the one patch of ice on the footway.
summaries.E64: Gaps discovered while drawing were declared on the sheets and never entered in `assumptions.json`, the file a reviewer receives.
summaries.E65: The headline number this proposal's self-criticism rests on was read off a sampled curve instead of computed, and sampling only ever understates a peak.
summaries.E66: A sheet claimed maintenance was already inside the annual operating band; the band counted re-survey sessions only.
summaries.E67: The commit that folded maintenance into the annual operating table left the same omission in the row directly beneath it, so one file priced two totals on two versions of the same model and set them side by side to be compared.
summaries.E68: A gate guarding the construction sheet against drift asserted seven dimensions and not the stone's own, while the mass those dimensions produce carried the whole maintenance argument.
summaries.E69: A gate searched the two editions concatenated, so a deliverable named only in Chinese passed as named in the prose.
summaries.E70: The errata register's own stated reason for existing was the last claim in the package nobody had re-measured, and the instrument that re-measured it matched on filename — counting who uses this package's word for a register, not who keeps one.
summaries.E71: A Chinese paragraph said the field shares are not repeated here because repeating them is how they expire; the English translation of that same paragraph repeated them, and by the time it was found they had expired.
summaries.E72: Three readings recomputed from the shipped layers every build are hand-copied into the prose — `412.5 m` six times. Nothing had gone wrong yet; the structure must eventually go wrong.
summaries.E73: The file built to prove the other gates can fail published a coverage number with no denominator: six of sixteen gates had been proven, and it read as all of them.
summaries.E74: Two sheets declared self-chosen dimensions in red on the drawing and nowhere in `assumptions.json`, the file a reviewer actually receives.
summaries.E75: Two gates were listed as unproven with a true reason, and the reason became nobody's action until the render cost was paid.
summaries.E76: The paragraph arguing that route lengths are not hand-written hand-wrote all six numbers derived from them, in both editions, in the same commit.
summaries.E77: Five entries in this register stated a live build quantity in the present tense, and three of them were already false — claims that had outlived their evidence, inside the register of claims that outlived their evidence.
summaries.E78: Every entry in this register is Chinese only, and the English edition cites five of them by number — sending a reader to text that does not exist in their language.
summaries.E79: E78 introduced the rule “publish the numerator and the denominator” and hand-wrote its own denominator, which E78's own existence had already made wrong.
summaries.E80: The harness that proves every gate can fail hard-coded its denominator as 16 against a real 15, and its arithmetic did not close: the gate it had never proven, never listed as unproven, and never counted was itself.
summaries.E81: FIG.30 flattened the paid year and stated the quarterly points need not move. Volunteers attend only the second and third order — exactly that tier — so the volunteer year stayed at a 31.0 h peak while the sheet declared the available lever worthless: true of the quantity it was measuring, false of this one.
summaries.E82: The head counts and hour bands the whole cost model runs on were never registered as assumptions — and the reverse index, which sees only `metrics.json`, was telling readers that nothing published rested on seven records that each drive a sheet.
summaries.E83: FIG.32 chose a participation cap when the package already stated one: personas.json describes community readers at a quarterly rhythm, and the chosen cap asked them for six visits a year — more than this proposal says they give.
summaries.E84: The width one standing person occupies was chosen twice under two names — an operator ring on one sheet, a shoulder on another — landing on the same 600 mm by coincidence, with two separate assumption records and nothing joining them.
summaries.E85: Two sheets' rules were copied into a third as literals, each with a comment naming where it came from. A comment that names a source is not a citation: it tells a reader where to look and does nothing when the source moves.
summaries.E86: Adding a thirty-third sheet pushed the English proposal 298 bytes past the 256 KiB intake cap. Every sheet costs prose in both editions and the English one runs longer, so it reaches the ceiling first — with 415 bytes left, the package can no longer add a sheet without trimming.
summaries.E87: A sentence claimed “the current corpus of 727” while the corpus stood at 793, and the staleness gate could not see it: that gate knows the corpus sizes this package has recorded, and 727 was never one — it was a one-off denominator. The phrase is the tell, not the value.
summaries.E88: E87's lesson turned on this package's own gates found the same shape in computed_value_qa: it checks nine quantities because someone wrote nine patterns, while metrics.json carries dozens the prose cites. The fix enumerates nothing — the suspicious values are read from git, since a value a metric used to hold is wrong by construction.
summaries.E89: A sheet that draws something almost always opens by saying the thing had never been drawn — true when written, false of the finished document. Four such sentences accumulated and three contradicted each other: FIG.26 called the second order the only tier never on a sheet, FIG.28 called the third order the only one never drawn, FIG.29 called the first order the last without a sheet. Only one can hold at a time and none holds of a package that draws all four. The register has carried the rule since E60 — a claim about something that moves must say when it was true — but it had never been pointed at the prose's claims about its own drawings, and nothing else could catch these because “only” is not a quantity anything computes. Found by reading, not by a gate. The fix requires scoping rather than banning the word: once every sentence says when, two of them can sit on the same page without fighting.
summaries.E90: FIG.24 labels each of seven device-envelope dimensions with the class of bound behind it — regulation, already published here, or chosen here — and the site speed of 6 km/h was classed as regulation, noted as following local rules the sheet did not set. A-DEVICE-002 went further and said in bold that v had a source where the reaction time and deceleration did not, which made FIG.26's 2.59 m halt distance read as one third grounded. No rule was ever named: none of the 22 sources covers device speed, the phrase appears nowhere outside assumptions.json, and no standard tag was ever attached, while every other external claim in this package cites an id. A rule nobody can look up is not distinguishable from a choice, and labelling one as regulation removes exactly the doubt a reader should apply. The value stands; the label is now 'chosen', the chosen count rises from three to four, both A-DEVICE derivations are rewritten so 2.59 m is entirely chosen rather than partly sourced, four hand-written copies of the count are now computed from the sheet's own table, and sources_qa.py refuses any bound whose declared class it cannot back.
summaries.E91: E90's question — where else does this package claim backing it cannot name? — was pointed at every other provenance claim. assumptions.json came back clean: its only six hits are E90's own sentences saying the opposite. The prose yielded exactly one more. The mandatory-measurement table tells a future operator to take noise limits from the national acoustic-environment standard for the zone, and none of the 22 sources is an acoustic standard; no instrument is named anywhere in either edition. This is milder than E90 because no number is printed, so nothing chosen is dressed as sourced — and worse in one way, because it is an instruction for someone else to carry out. That row exists precisely because the field's qualitative 'noise nuisance' cannot determine exceedance; an instruction to use the standard value without naming the standard cannot either. No citation was invented to close it: the standard was never obtained, so the sentence now says so, in both editions. The gate extends from FIG.24's table to the prose, narrowed to claims about limits rather than about obligations, and accepts either a resolving id or the admission.
summaries.E92: E90's own fix created this. Before the relabel, FIG.24 said the site speed followed local regulation and that the sheet set no number, while two scope declarations said the package gives no speed figure and does not decide device speed limits - three sentences in agreement. E90 reclassified the bound as chosen here, correctly, since no regulation could be named; that made the other two false, because the package now does fix a speed, states it on the sheet, registers it as A-DEVICE-001 and derives FIG.26's 2.59 m halt distance from it. Four sentences across two editions. Worse, the tick that made the change examined one of them and recorded that it had survived scrutiny - the reasoning ran backwards, since labelling a value as chosen means the package gives it, which is what the sentence denied, and that wrong conclusion was carried forward as a premise. The fix is not to retract E90 but to draw the distinction that should have been there: no statutory limit, which belongs to the authority, and a site operating bound of 6 km/h that this package admits is its own. A gate now watches the seam, requiring any out-of-scope paragraph naming a chosen bound to say it is chosen here. Its scope is stated: it sees paragraphs that name the bound, not ones referring to it by category such as 'device speed limits', which are held by prose discipline instead - a synonym list would look wider and be the list-dependent check this register keeps warning about. Also recorded: that gate's first version reduced the bound to its digits and reported two paragraphs that merely contained the numeral, the third time a first-draft gate here has been too broad; and the mutation written to prove it first struck prose the gate does not cover, damaging nothing, the fourth time that has happened.
summaries.E93: figure_citation_qa.py exists on the argument that a deliverable nobody is sent to is a deliverable nobody opens, and enforced it against a hand-written list of seven names. Three shipped assets were not on it. gate_mutation.json, 22 KB, appears in neither edition in any form - not the filename, not the argument - and it holds the twenty deliberate defects proving twelve of fifteen gates can fail, this package's strongest single piece of evidence about its own checks. claim_audit.json appears in neither. agent_declarations.json, at 89 KB the largest shipped asset, appears in Chinese only, so an English-reading reviewer was never told it exists - the same defect this gate's own comments record the mutation harness catching once before, for a different file, returned somewhere the list did not reach. That matters more than it looks because scripts/review_submission.py does not read visual/assets/ at all: a sentence in the prose is the only route by which a reviewer learns any of these exists. Twenty-five of twenty-eight assets were already named in both editions, so the convention was real and three files had fallen out of it. All three are now named in both, and the list is gone: must_name() reads every visual/assets/*.json from the directory and joins it to the five products, taking the check from seven names to thirty-three and growing it automatically with each new asset.
summaries.E94: The shipped metrics.json said errata_entry_count = 92 while the shipped errata.json held 93 and both editions of the prose said 93. metrics.json and proposal.md are both among the nine files the review pipeline reads whole, so the contradiction was visible in one sitting without opening anything else. It was not a typo but an ordering: recompute_metrics.py runs second in the build because geometry feeds it, and eleven of its metrics count a shipped artifact - errata entries, scenario cards, rights-ledger rows, taskbook requirements - every one of which is written later in the same build. Those eleven therefore read the previous build's files and lagged by exactly one build whenever an artifact changed; only the errata count showed it because only that artifact had changed. computed_value_qa checked nine hand-listed quantities and errata_entry_count was not among them, the fifth time a list-shaped check has missed what was not on its list. The ordering is repaired by a second metric pass once the artifacts exist, and the gate takes no list: it asserts the stronger and simpler property that recomputing the file changes nothing, so any future reordering or any new artifact-counting metric fails here instead of in a reviewer's hands. Also recorded: this check's first version exited on its first finding, which stopped the gate before its other checks reported - caught at once by the mutation harness, since M16 expects this gate to name 9,443 and the early exit hid it. A gate that stops at its first finding conceals the rest.
summaries.E95: census_claims_qa's fourteen facts must each be found, but its twenty-one context patterns work the other way: they constrain every occurrence of a phrasing, so zero occurrences is zero constraint. The loop never runs, nothing is reported, and the summary line kept saying twenty-one context patterns as though each had done work. Three had silently stopped checking. Two were decay rather than design error - the patterns are pinned to exact wording and the prose around them is rewritten constantly, so every reword is a chance for one to fall silent while the headline number holds steady; that is the constraint-that-cannot-be-failed shape this register already carries under constraint-that-cannot-be-failed, arriving by erosion. The third was not decay but a real asymmetry: the English frontmatter summary had never carried the census claim at all. The Chinese says seventeen re-runnable censuses, 184 to 793, every reading shipped - the most distinctive sentence in the package - while the English said only that measured findings were produced. That summary is the first prose an English reviewer meets and is rendered at the top of report/proposal.en.html, one of the two pages screenshotted for the review model. Now a pattern matching nothing in scope fails the build, and the gate reports the occurrences it actually constrained rather than the patterns it declares. The robotics pattern is retired since a second pattern already covers the current wording, the youth-friendly one is repointed, and the English summary states the claim - paid for by trading vaguer words for specific ones, with the English edition down to its last bytes.
summaries.E96: Fourteen section headings stamp themselves with a requirement id, and two rows of taskbook_coverage.json cite such a heading as evidence for a different requirement: the landmarks section, headed agent.4, answers agent.5's spatial culture system, and the honours-and-components section, also headed agent.4, answers agent.6's developer community mechanism. Neither is wrong - a landmark is a cultural expression carrier and an honours system is a community mechanism, so both sections genuinely serve two requirements while their headings name only the one they were written for. The cost falls on the reader: someone checking where agent.5 is answered lands on a heading stamped agent.4 and concludes it is not, which is a brief_alignment reading of a package that does answer it - and brief_alignment is exactly where two rivals moved this week. This package argues constantly that claiming coverage is not coverage; this is the mirror image, covering something in a way nobody can see, and it costs the same. The fix discloses rather than retitles: the coverage file now reads each heading's own id and, when it differs from the requirement being evidenced, says so in the shipped row. Retitling would also remove the inconsistency but would erase the true fact that the section was written for agent.4; disclosure keeps more. No mutation guards this and the reason is published: the one written for it stripped the heading id and the gate stayed silent, which on inspection was the gate being right - a heading that no longer claims agent.4 leaves nothing ambiguous to disclose, so that edit removes the ambiguity rather than hiding it. Recorded alongside: this tick set out to judge whether 18 percent of the document spent on design basis starves the taskbook chapters, and the answer is no - all 63 requirements are decided by code rather than declared, evidence strength is graded honestly in three tiers, and the thinnest section is 682 characters of specific decisions.
summaries.E97: claim_audit_qa holds every unit-carrying number to multiset parity across the two editions, and its vocabulary was ten units - percent, hectare, square metre, kilogram, kilometre, yuan, CNY, minute, hour, metre - with millimetre absent. The metre pattern cannot match it either, because the word boundary fails on the second m. So twenty-eight millimetre measurements per edition fell entirely outside the check: the FIG.24 device envelope, the KIT stone at 400 by 400 by 600, the reading-plate cap heights, FIG.25's 2,400 mm setup circle. The summary line said seventy-three unit-carrying measurements, same set in both editions, which reads as covering the measurements in the prose. Those millimetre values are the most-edited dimensions in the package - E90 reclassified the 6 km/h site speed and E92 rewrote four scope declarations because of it, both errata circling this family of numbers - and they had never been held to parity. A check whose headline claims one set is as wide as its vocabulary decides, not as wide as the prose. Millimetre, second, km/h and km² are now in it, ordered so the longer units match before the shorter ones, and the audited set rises from 73 to 80. To be exact: no drift was found - the two editions' millimetre multisets are identical - so this raises a floor rather than repairing a defect, and is recorded as such.
summaries.E98: The errata register's tense gate carried a rule that a fraction N over M counts this register whenever M sits within three of the number of entries, and such a count must name the moment it was true. When the register reached 97 entries that window swallowed 100 - the denominator of every score and every percentage - and the build failed on E35's score 91/100 and its seven-dimension weighted 91.0/100, and on E79's list of 91/100, 354/106 and 16/18. All of those are historical review scores, and E79's own sentence says such numbers are exactly what a historical record should carry. This is a trap that arms itself as the register grows: not one character in those entries changed, the register simply got bigger, and the check's correctness had been resting on a numeric coincidence. Requiring the denominator to equal the entry count exactly would only postpone the collision to the day this register holds a hundred entries. A denominator cannot say what is being counted. The proximity proxy is gone and the check now keys on the claim form, because a count of this register names what it counts - the same move E87 recorded. Four cases were verified: a live register count still fails, a count scoped to its moment passes, and both review scores pass.
summaries.E99: E98's question - does this check's correctness rest on a numeric coincidence that changes as the package grows - was put to every other gate, and found three families of hard-coded digit widths. census_claims_qa's nine corpus patterns write three digits, while the corpus has run 184 to 793 and is still rising; at four digits they fail two different ways, capturing 000 out of 1000 and reporting a drift that does not exist, or matching nothing at all. build_errata finds cited entries with a two-digit pattern, so at E100 the word boundary fails and the check requiring an English summary for every cited entry silently stops covering anything above ninety-nine - and this register holds 98 entries, two short of that. The figure pattern is worse than a miss: it captures 10 out of FIG.100, so the gate would report FIG.10 as cited and FIG.100 as uncited, wrong in both directions. None of these is a typo; each treats a digit width as a constant while the thing it counts grows. E98 was this shape firing for real when the register reached 97; pointing the same question elsewhere found the next ones before they fired. All are now minimum widths with no maximum. Both gates still pass unchanged, so this raises a floor rather than repairing a live defect, and says so. E95's new rule - a pattern matching nothing fails the build - already guarded the silent half of this family; the false-positive half had nothing watching it until now.
summaries.E100: forward_reference_qa had been published as unprovable by mutation, on the reason that its defect is a direction - a reference that resolves and points the wrong way - and so needs a reordering rather than a swap. That reason is wrong. The body citation of mechanism rule 4 is lawful precisely because it announces its direction, saying the full definition appears below; deleting that announcement is a single-string swap which leaves the sentence grammatical and the reference resolving, while making it point forward in silence. The gate caught it at once and named the line and the rule. This is the second time a published unprovable reason described the first tactic tried rather than the gate itself - census_claims_qa was the first, closed by M23. A reason makes a gap honest; it does not make it real. Publishing the uncovered gates with their reasons was meant to stop a gap being quietly omitted, but the reasons are themselves claims and have to be audited like any other, or they become present-tense assertions about this package that nobody will re-measure - the shape E89 records. Twenty-five deliberate defects now prove 14 of 15 gates. The one remaining is the mutation harness itself, which cannot byte-swap its own detection and instead runs a control mutation that no gate should catch, refusing to continue if that comes back caught: a principled exception rather than an untried one. A coincidence worth recording: this entry is E100, the first id the old two-digit citation scanner could not have seen. E99 widened it one entry before it mattered and added an assertion feeding every held id to that same pattern, so this entry is that fix's first beneficiary.
summaries.E101: E100's rule - a published reason is itself a claim and must be audited - was turned on every place this package publishes a reason for a limitation, and the first was claim_audit_qa's exemption tables. ALLOW_PARITY held eight entries, each naming a number permitted to differ between the editions and each with a written justification: 2026, 2023, the identifier suffixes 001 through 004, and the railway's 1913 and 1909. All eight were already inert. This gate had moved from blocking on bare numbers to blocking only on numbers carrying a unit, and from that moment years and identifier suffixes were no longer in the compared set at all. The exemptions outlived the change that made them unnecessary and shipped in claim_audit.json as allowlist_parity, presented to a reviewer as the eight exceptions this check requires. A dead exemption is not clutter, it is armed: should any of those values ever appear as a unit-carrying measurement in one edition only, the entry would excuse it in silence - the same armed-and-waiting shape as E99's digit widths, in an allowlist instead of a regex. And in the shipped file they made a check that needs no exemptions read as a check exempted eight times. The table is now empty, which is the stronger claim, and an assertion fails the build on any exemption whose key is in both editions or neither - E95's rule for patterns that match nothing, applied to allowlists. A second table, ALLOW_COPY, turned out to be referenced by nothing that runs; it belongs to the check designed and not shipped, and is renamed to say so. Proven by direct test rather than by the mutation harness, with the reason stated: the tables live in analysis/, which is not in the submitted package, and the harness only damages shipped files.
summaries.E102: The reason sweep continued into claim_audit_qa's check that was designed and not shipped - the one forbidding a number inside a generated block from also being typed into the prose beside it. The reason holds: 76 candidate occurrences across 39 distinct values, and every one is a figure this package computes, with the check genuinely unable to separate a generated sentence from a hand-written one. But following that reason turned up what the declined check would have been for. Four of those 39 values exist in no shipped JSON at all: 83.5 h and 7.5 h, FIG.30's peak and trough and the whole basis of its eleven-to-one claim; 1,111 m, FIG.21's worst walk; and 14.0 m, FIG.33's benchmark clearance. computed_value_qa did not cover them and stale_against_history cannot see them either, because it walks shipped files. So those four sentences had no verification path of any kind. FIG.33 asserts its own 14.0 m at build time, but the prose copy was tied to nothing; change FIG.30's model and the peak and trough stay on the page in silence. A declined check having a sound reason does not mean the thing it guarded against is guarded elsewhere - that is the step easiest to skip when auditing a reason. FIG.30's three figures are now checked, imported from fig_year rather than retyped, taking the verified set from 9 quantities to 13 and from 21 hand-written statements to 33. The remaining two are recorded as not done rather than claimed: 1,111 m and 14.0 m need their sheets to expose the value as a function, which is a structural change left for the next step. Also recorded: this check's first draft keyed on the bare word peak, which FIG.31 uses for the volunteer peak, so it read 31.0 and 23.0 and reported two sheets sharing a noun as a drift - the fourth first-draft gate here to be too broad, and every time the gate was right and the pattern wrong.
summaries.E103: E102 found four figures in the prose with no verification path of any kind, repaired three of them, and recorded the other two as outstanding rather than letting the fix imply full coverage: FIG.21's 1,111 m, the worst walk on the line to the nearest benchmark, and FIG.33's 14.0 m, the clearance from the mobility hub to BM-302. This entry finishes them. Both are cases where the sheet computes the value and reasons from it at build time - FIG.21 uses the distance to decide that the fifteen-minute rule fails, FIG.33 checks that no benchmark falls inside a building footprint - while the sentences quoting the number, six of them for 1,111 m and four for 14.0 m across the two editions, were connected to that computation by nothing at all. Neither value appears in a shipped JSON, so the history check could not reach them either, since it walks shipped files. A gap declared outstanding is only honest if the next step actually closes it; otherwise the declaration just makes the debt look tidy. fig_reach now exposes worst_walk() and fig_station exposes clearance(), both imported by computed_value_qa rather than retyped, and both sheets' main() calls the same function, so the drawing and the prose cannot compute it separately. The verified set rises from 13 quantities to 15 and from 33 hand-written statements to 46, and all four of E102's figures now have a path. Following the previous entry's lesson, the wording was grepped before the patterns were written: each of the ten sentences uses phrasing unique to its sheet, so no second figure shares a noun this time.
summaries.E104: The reason sweep reached the shipped manifest_schema_survey.json, whose resolution_zh announced that this package's four previously declared schema exceptions were all void and that it now declares zero. The same file's this_package.declared_exceptions listed one, and its violations count said one: a shipped JSON saying zero in one field and listing one in another. The four voided exceptions were all role exceptions, and the package later acquired an exception of a different kind, unexpected_property_at_root:data_confidence, so the unqualified sentence was overtaken by its own data. What makes it worth recording is the sentence immediately after it, which says that a survey still reporting numbers the schema can no longer produce is the register's own claim-outlived-the-package shape - an accurate description of the sentence before it. The warning and the thing warned against were adjacent. The difference between the two fields was only that declared_exceptions is computed while the word zero was remembered, so this is also the register's rule against hand-writing a count the build can read, broken by the register itself. Fixed by scoping rather than deleting, as E89 prescribes: the sentence now says the four role exceptions were voided and role exceptions stood at zero after that fix, then reports the current totals computed from the same data the declared_exceptions field uses, so the two cannot diverge again. An assertion was added because the paragraph's opening claim - that this survey's violation class can no longer occur - holds only while role really is an open pattern upstream: that is measured on every run, and a reversion now fails the build with its reason.
summaries.E105: Auditing the preconditions on metrics.json's two unknown metrics found the preconditions themselves sound - approved FAR controls and the official boundary are not public, and neither is the ownership and existing-conditions survey - but the three prose explanations in that file were each in one language, and not the same one. floor_area_ratio's reason was English, existing_residential_floor_area_sqm's was a 200-character Chinese paragraph, and evidence_class_note was Chinese. metrics.json is one of the nine files the reviewing model receives whole, so each reviewer could read some of its explanations and not others. The Chinese paragraph happens to carry the most interesting judgement in the file - why land-use codes 0701 and 0804 are absent from land_use.geojson, falling inside the eleven deliberately blank blocks whose boundaries depend on the same unpublished data, a judgement rather than an omission - and an English reader saw none of it. This is the asymmetry E93 and E95 record for the two proposal editions, occurring where nothing was watching: cjk_leak_qa scans English artifacts and parity_qa compares the proposals, and no gate reads the explanatory text inside a shipped JSON. All three now exist in both languages, and a build assertion requires it of any explanatory field, derived from the fields themselves rather than from a list. formula is excluded with the trade named: it is an expression, not prose, and translating a division of two symbols adds nothing. The assertion was checked on four cases - English-only and Chinese-only both fail, either language with its counterpart passes.
summaries.E106: Generalising E105, every shipped JSON was swept for prose carried in one language only. The sweep flagged 38 files and most of that was false positive: census.json's quoted fields are other proposals' own Chinese text, where translating would falsify the quotation; errata.json's Chinese fields already pair with an English summary; licence names and script paths are not prose. One finding was real, and it is the one that matters most. sources.json is both a file the reviewing model receives whole and the registry every external claim in this package resolves against - E90 and E91 are entirely about citing sources by a resolvable id - and all 22 of its titles were Chinese only, as were all 22 collection methods and all 22 licence terms, with usage mixed 15 to 7. Twelve of the entries are Chinese laws, ministry measures and a State Council notice, where the title is the only field saying which instrument is meant. An English-reading reviewer checking a citation could see its id and its url and not what the source is: the reference resolves and still cannot be checked. All 22 now carry title_en, using the instruments' official English names, and sources_qa requires a non-empty one of every record. Scope is stated rather than implied: collection_method, licence terms and the Chinese half of usage remain Chinese-only and were not translated in this pass. They describe how this package handled a source rather than which source it is, so the loss is the smaller one - but it is a loss, recorded here instead of left for a reader to find.
summaries.E107: E106 gave all 22 sources an English title and recorded three fields as outstanding: collection_method, Chinese in all 22 records, license_or_reuse_terms, likewise all 22, and the Chinese half of usage, 15 of 22. This entry finishes them. The title says which source is meant; these three say how it was obtained, what may be reused and what this package does with it - which is what judging the strength of a piece of evidence actually rests on. Several carry self-corrections a reader would otherwise never reach. The collection note for the regulatory-detailed-planning measure records that checking the text corrected a statement in this package: the measure contains no article enumerating mandatory content, so the matrix line about it is this proposal's own paraphrase rather than the regulation's wording. The OSM licence note records that this package does redistribute an extracted subset of the original data - 275 vertices constituting a Derivative Database under ODbL - and that the field previously claimed otherwise, which stopped being true once the coordinates shipped. Those are exactly the admissions an English reviewer should see, and none of them reached one. All three fields now carry English counterparts, and the sources_qa assertion widens from title alone to all four: a Chinese value with no English counterpart fails the build, while a field already in English needs none, decided from the value rather than from a list of names. The summary line now reports the 88 fields actually compared rather than the record count - its first version said 88 of 22 sources, counting fields while speaking of records. sources.json stands at 48,570 bytes, 464 KiB under the per-file cap, and E106 has no outstanding items left.
summaries.E108: E100's rule was turned on the scope statements this package writes into its own gates. The register keeps insisting a check must state what it covers, which makes every such statement a claim awaiting audit. Two failed, in opposite directions. One was too wide: figure_citation_qa's must_name said every shipped asset is named in both editions while the code globbed only visual/assets/*.json, leaving the nine geometry layers, the five shipped .js verifiers and the JSONs outside that directory unchecked. Measuring found all of them already named in both editions - so the claim was true of the package and guaranteed by nothing, a coincidence being reported as a rule, which is E99's lesson that widening is not the guarantee and the guarantee is that nobody has to remember. The other was too narrow, and worse: the scope note E106 wrote into sources_qa said collection_method, licence terms and the Chinese half of usage were not checked and remained Chinese-only - and E107 closed exactly that the next day, adding 22, 22 and 15 English counterparts and widening the check from one field to four. A note describing a limitation that no longer exists is the claim-outlived-the-package shape this register carries eight times, and it survived a tick inside the gate whose own docstring argues against it. The wide claim is fixed by widening the code: must_name now covers every shipped .json, .geojson and .js, taking checked deliverables from 33 to 58, all passing, turning a coincidence into an enforcement. PNG and SVG are excluded because a figure is reached through the drawing index and the per-sheet citation check, a stronger route than being named once; PDF, Markdown and HTML are the products already listed. Both exclusions are reachability arguments rather than conveniences. The narrow claim is fixed by correcting the sentence and keeping the old one, as the register requires.
summaries.E109: The last published unprovable reason was the mutation harness's own. It said this file cannot mutate its own detection with a byte-swap and so runs a control mutation no gate should catch - and that control exercises one half of the detection line, code != 0, and nothing else. The other half, named, which asks whether the gate actually named the damage it caught, was touched by no control at all, while this file printed on every run that every defect was caught and named by the gate that caught it. Half of its own headline rested on code nothing tested. That half does real work: six mutations this session were misaimed and revealed only because must_name failed to match - 2,400 where the gate normalises separators to 2400, and a Chinese article reference where the gate reports in English - so had named been quietly true, all six would have been recorded as clean catches. This is the third time a published unprovable reason described one approach rather than the gate, after census_claims_qa and forward_reference_qa. A second control now creates damage the gate genuinely catches while demanding a name no gate could print, and requires the harness to classify it as not caught; breaking named to a constant makes that control fail, which was tested and then reverted. The uncovered reason is narrowed and the old sentence kept: what remains is not that detection cannot be proven but that no shipped-file mutation can reach this file, because analysis/ is excluded from the package by intake - a fact about the package boundary rather than a property of the code.
summaries.E110: The audit of my own scope statements reached E105's exclusion of formula from the rule that explanations must exist in both languages. Its stated reason was that a formula is an expression rather than prose, and that translating a division of two symbols would say nothing the symbols do not. That is true of 34 of the 36 metrics and false of two: one read sum(existing_residential_floor_area) within the design scope, the other count(...) followed by a clause saying it shares one definition with matrix_refs_qa.count_references. Each is an expression plus a sentence the symbols cannot say, and the second is a provenance claim of exactly the kind this package treats as load-bearing. An exclusion whose reason covers only part of what it excludes leaves the rest excluded for no stated reason. The rule also carried a two-name list of the fields it checked, which is the shape this register keeps removing - and a third explanatory field, formula_note, was added the same day and would have been exempt by omission. The fix does not widen the exclusion to cover prose it never argued for; it makes the data fit the sentence. Both formulas are now pure expressions and their clauses live in formula_note with a counterpart in the other language, a field the rule does check, so the exclusion holds by construction rather than by exception - a guard made unnecessary beating a guard that passes. The checked set is now derived from the fields themselves rather than named, and the rule was verified in both directions by omitting the English half on purpose and watching the build refuse. Also recorded: the first edit was made to metrics.json, which recompute_metrics rewrites on every run - change a value where it lives, the same lesson M25 taught.
summaries.E111: Auditing the reason E102 published for not shipping the hand-copy check found the core argument sound - the check cannot tell a generated sentence from a hand-written one, which is the only distinction that would make its findings mean anything - while the paragraph around it carried two hard-coded numbers and both had gone stale. It said the check reported 67 candidates where the run now reports 76, and that the register carried that shape fifteen times where it carries 23. Sweeping for the same shape found six more places copying the register's own tallies into comments and shipped text: fig_phasing, fig_riverfront, spatial_level_survey, census_claims_qa and two in build_errata, one of those inside E95's shipped English summary. Four times where the live count is 14, twice where it is 7. Every copy had drifted. None was wrong when written. All were numbers this package computes on every build, transcribed into prose that nothing recomputes - the rule against hand-writing a count the build can read, broken inside reasons, which is precisely what E100 says must be audited like any other claim. The fix deletes the numbers rather than updating them, because updating only rewinds the clock: that is E98's trap, where aiming a window at the present merely postpones the collision to the next round of growth. The candidate count is printed live by the gate's own report line and the shape tallies are computed and published by the register, which prints a repeated-shapes line every build. All seven now name the shape and omit the count - keeping the part a reader can check and dropping the part that expires.
summaries.E112: Applying the new rule - check a reason's numbers before judging its argument - to assumptions.json found the numbers entirely clean: all ten counted claims match the live values, including the corpus at 793 with its census date attached, the 22 sources, and FIG.32's 88, 24, 8, 4 and 22, all agreeing with what the build prints. The arguments were not. A-ROSTER-001's next_action, in both languages, still said that until the gap closes the half is chosen here - while two other fields of the same record say the opposite. Its statement reads that the cap is not chosen by the sheet, and its derivation reads that this record has no self-chosen value at all, explicitly recording that the earlier half-a-point's-sessions rule was replaced by the four-a-year rhythm read from personas.json. One record, shipped whole to the reviewer, disagreeing with itself: two fields saying the chosen value is gone and a third still treating it as current. This is E104's shape again - a note outliving the very fix it sits beside - and the gap it described had not disappeared but changed content, which the stale wording concealed: four a year is read from a persona file this package wrote, not from an outside rule. Both halves of next_action now say what is actually still owed, keeping the gap and dropping the dead reference. The new numbers-first rule earned itself on first use by separating a case where every figure was right and the reasoning had expired, which a single verdict on the record would have passed.
summaries.E113: The last target of the reason sweep was sources_qa's AUTHORITATIVE and NOT_OBTAINED reasoning. Numbers first, and they were right: 22 records, and both defects the comment describes - grading the maintainers' provisional boundary geometry as official context while its own source_type called it inferred, and grading a document regulatory_baseline while its retrieved_at said not obtained - are fixed and written in the past tense. The problem was the test itself. NOT_OBTAINED was a three-phrase list, and it caught the single wording this file currently uses while missing Not obtained capitalised, not yet obtained, an em dash and n/a, each of which says the same thing. A record whose retrieved_at read any of those could be graded regulatory_baseline while nobody had opened the document, which is precisely the grade this check exists to refuse. The gap was also widening rather than closing: E106 and E107 had just made this file bilingual, so a future not-obtained marker is now as likely to be written in English as in Chinese, and the list leaned Chinese - two correct fixes that together pushed an older test somewhere it could not reach. retrieved_at is either the day the document was read or it is not, so the test is now whether it parses as a date: no list, and nothing to out-word. The old phrases are kept in the comment with the reason they were once enough. Verified in both directions by setting a regulatory_baseline record's retrieved_at to the English Not obtained, which the old list would certainly have passed, and watching the gate name it. That completes the reason sweep: nine reasons examined, seven defective, two recorded as sound.
summaries.E114: Auditing the last two list-shaped gates found that matrix_refs_qa's REFERENCE_FIELDS named fourteen fields while the three matrices actually carry fifteen list-of-string fields. The missing one was completeness_limited_by, so none of its references had ever been resolved - and that field holds the matrices' most consequential admission: what limits a given depth item. development_intensity_controls is limited by the metric floor_area_ratio, and two further items by the source MOHURD-ARCH-DESIGN-DEPTH-2016: a metric key and a source id, both genuine references. All of them resolve today, so nothing was broken and this raises a floor rather than repairing a live defect, which is recorded as such. But a rename on either side would have dangled in silence, in precisely the field a reviewer consults to see what a depth item is missing - the reference still present, the thing it points at gone, which is the single failure this gate exists to prevent. The field was exempt because it was absent from a list, not because anyone judged it needed no checking. It is now registered with a resolver of its own, since it is the only field drawing on two id spaces - a metric key when a number is missing, a source id when a document is - so it resolves against either and nothing else; a one-letter typo still fails, which was tested. Resolved references rise from 523 to 526, all of them resolved, where the three had not previously even been counted. And the list is not merely longer: a new assertion requires every list-of-string field actually present in the matrices to be either registered or declared to hold no references, with a reason. A future field must be judged once rather than exempted by omission, which is exactly how this one slipped through.
summaries.E115: Auditing the last list-shaped gate, assumption_refs_qa: all 38 assumption ids resolve, and the second reference space the gate itself stands on - source_files - had never been resolved at all. Rule 4's entire verdict is a substring test against paths nobody had checked exist, so a single misspelt letter made from_corpus quietly false: the metric is not flagged, it is exempted, and the exemption is invisible. The rule written because resolving is not the same as being right was resting on references that were never resolved. Resolving them showed a second thing: 34 of the 35 paths are relative to the submission and one, the organiser's published planning limits, is relative to the repository root - both resolve, in different roots, and metrics.json goes to the reviewer whole. The heavier finding was in evidence_ceiling.class_of, where an unregistered source defaulted to self_measured, the middle of a five-step order and two steps above background_only. So the single thing that file exists to prevent - a number stated above the strength of what it reads - was what the default produced: name a scraped table or a hand-typed figure in source_files and the ceiling it implies is a count of this package, with the build green. The default failed open, in the direction of the claim, and it needed no new file: census_history.json and manifest_schema_survey.json were already shipping, already readings of other people's work, and unregistered. The default is gone. An unregistered path now stops the build, names itself and lists the five classes, which is the same correction E114 made: a decision made once beats an exemption by omission. Both census files are registered as background_only. assumption_refs_qa now resolves every source path - in the package, or under an explicitly declared outside-the-package prefix with a note on what it is - and only a metric with no value may read nothing, since naming no source exempts a number from every source rule below. The readout is 43 source paths, all resolving: 42 in the package, 1 in the organiser's brief. All three checks were verified in both directions by a one-letter path typo, by emptying a valued metric's sources, and by pointing one at an unregistered file.
summaries.E116: The same file said two opposite things about the same seven numbers. The evidence ceiling graded 17 metrics provisional - a grade this package assigns for exactly one reason, that the layer read is drawn on the inferred boundary - while only 11 of them cited A-BOUNDARY-001. The sharpest pair: benchmark_count cited it and benchmark_first_order_count, a count of the same features in the same layer, did not. The citation had always been decided by hand at each call site, correctly 11 times and not at all the other 7. For those seven a reader was told the number is provisional and not told what makes it so, which is the two-copies-drifted shape this register has logged three times. A-BOUNDARY-001's own impact clause settles which copy was right: siting conclusions are provisional too, and the official data requires the whole thing to be recomputed rather than one file swapped, so a count of features in a layer that must be redrawn as a whole is exactly such a conclusion. The hand-made version was the wrong one. The citation is now derived from the computed class rather than remembered: every metric graded provisional carries the assumption, which makes the 11 hand-passed arguments redundant rather than load-bearing. Id references rise from 38 to 45 and the assumption's reverse index from 11 to 18. The gate gains an exact rule - graded provisional means citing the assumption - with its scope stated: only that direction is required, and the converse neither holds nor should, since floor_area_ratio has no value and reads the organiser's limits, so its class is official_context while it still rests on the boundary the ratio would be taken against. One more list was dissolved in the same place: the prose test read assumptions and reason only, while the record has since grown reason_zh, reason_en, both formula notes and both evidence-class notes. A bilingual split moves prose out of the field an older check reads, which is how E113's test went stale; the test now reads every string in the record. Nothing had drifted out of reach yet, and now nothing can. The failing direction needed no mutation: run against the file as it stood, the gate named all seven.
summaries.E117: The two editions gave opposite answers to how the 63 requirements split. The Chinese read 32 must-address and 31 required outputs; the English, 31 must-address items and 32 required outputs - the same two counts, exchanged. The build counts them: of the 63 rows in taskbook_coverage.json, 32 are must_address_zh and 31 required_outputs, so the Chinese was right. The passage carrying the error is the one whose argument is that a claim of coverage is not coverage. Both editions go to the reviewer whole, so this is not an internal typo but one package giving two numbers for one fact, in the paragraph it uses to fault others for asserting coverage instead of joining to it. What matters more is why it survived: these are numbers the build computes, and this package has a standing rule that a prose number the build computes joins computed_value_qa in the same commit. These two never did, so nothing had ever compared them against the data. The rule was right and simply had not been followed here. The English is corrected to 32 and 31, at identical byte count so the English headroom is untouched, and both counts now join the checked set - counted from the shipped file rather than retyped, following the standing preference for an import over a value with a comment naming its source. Checked statements rise from 46 to 50 and checked quantities from 15 to 17. The failing direction used the real pre-fix text: restoring the swap made the gate name both, computed as 32 where the prose said 31 and its dual, after which the text was put back.
summaries.E118: Comparing the numbers in the two editions one by one led to a single paragraph: the one about checking the three matrices' references. That paragraph gave two answers for one quantity. Its first sentence read 523 declared and 523 resolving, citing metric:matrix_reference_count; its second said the matrices assert 114 times. 114 was the reference count on the day the sentence was written - the commit that wrote it is titled with that number - and when the count grew to 523 only the first sentence was updated. E114 then raised it to 526, and all four statements across both editions stayed behind. The English had both numbers as 523, so it was internally consistent and equally stale. The cause is the citation itself: [metric:x] looks like a join and resolved to nothing. There are 37 such citations across the two editions and no check had ever read one, so the name could be misspelt or the metric deleted and the sentence would go on citing it - a reference that resolves to nothing while reading as evidence, which is the objection this package makes everywhere else, sitting inside the notation invented to demonstrate the opposite. When E114 moved the metric, nothing existed that could speak. All four statements now read 526, at identical byte count in both editions, and matrix_reference_count is read from metrics.json and joined to each of the four - the same standing rule E117 had just paid for, that a prose number the build computes joins the checked set in the same commit. A second, exact gate requires every [metric:x] in either edition to name a metric that exists: 37 citations, all resolving, and a one-letter typo fails, which was tested. Checked statements rise from 50 to 54. The gate's own arithmetic was also wrong: it appended two assertion lines to the same list whose length it reported as the number of quantities checked, so that figure had always run one high - the 15 to 17 recorded in E117 was, after this correction, 14 to 16 - and the summary strings those assertions returned were computed and never shown, so they are now printed on their own lines. The failing direction used the real pre-fix text: restored to 523 and 114, the gate named both.
summaries.E119: Continuing the number-by-number comparison of the two editions. 240 appears three times in Chinese and twice in English, and the difference is in the green-corridor paragraph. The Chinese reads: the corridor is a 120 m buffer each side of the spine (240 m wide - the earlier phrase 120 m corridor read as the full width when it is the half). The English dropped that correction entirely, and its own sentence used precisely the wording being corrected: a 120 m buffer of the spine, which reads as the full width. A correction written in one language only is no correction to the reader of the other, and what went missing was not a flourish but a misreading this package had owned up to: the English reader still had the sentence that misleads, with nothing anywhere saying it had once been wrong. The fallback was checked and there is none - neither this nor the 0.2025 to 0.1966 correction appears in the errata register at all, both living only in prose, so the English reader had no second route. The English table row in the same passage does say 240 m wide, but a number appearing in a table is not the same as the sentence having been corrected. The English now reads that the corridor buffers the spine 120 m each side, 240 m wide, and that the old wording read as the full width - giving the English reader both the width and the fact that it had been misread. The edition stood at 262,047 bytes with 97 of headroom; this edit is 13 bytes, leaving 84, and the headroom was computed before the sentence was written rather than after. The full sweep is recorded as it ran: 373 distinct numbers across the two editions, 55 differing in count, 7 of them appearing in one edition only - 114 closed by E118, and the colour table accounting for most of the rest, where Chinese renders the contrast figures as a table and English as a sentence with no content missing - and 47 differing in count for the ordinary reason that Chinese uses digits where English uses words. A broad sweep is a lead generator and not a verdict: of the 47, exactly one was real.
summaries.E120: The proposal spends a paragraph on a published contract nobody enforces: the site package ships manifest.schema.json, every submission ships a manifest.json, 79 of 825 do not satisfy it, and validate_submission.py checks only that declared files exist with matching digests. So what about this package? Six schemas are published, and this package validated against exactly one of them - manifest, whose exceptions it tracked by kind - and had never read the other five. Measured against upstream's current schemas, three files failed: self_check.json on generated_by, and both standard_matrix.json and design_depth_matrix.json on reviewer_reachability_total. Every one of the three was a key this package had added itself; metrics and compliance happened to be clean. Pointing at a contract others do not enforce while not enforcing it here, and failing on one's own additions, is the plainest form of the rule this register calls applied-to-others-but-not-to-self. It was not upstream's doing: the organisers' scaffold puts data_confidence inside validation_claim, where the schema allows it, and this package had written a second copy at the root, where it does not. One more thing belongs in the record. The first run of this check read the copy of brief/ in this repository and reported 36 manifest errors, 34 of them role-enum violations - the exact thing Issue #1058 fixed on 2026-08-11 by making role an open pattern, which this proposal's own text describes. This branch is based before #2149, so its brief/ is old, and a conformance check reading an expired contract reports the contract's history rather than the package's state. That wrong sentence came close to being written here. Two redundant keys are gone: generated_by, which named what produced a file that the register and the proposal both already name, and the root data_confidence, whose removal takes this package's manifest exceptions to zero. Two are kept and declared with the trade stated in code: reviewer_reachability_total in both matrices, because deleting it would pass the check by moving evidence out of the three files of that family the review pipeline reads whole and into visual/assets, which it does not read.
